config.title: Image Lazy Loading

intro.title: Image Lazy Loading
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React component that displays a list of images with lazy loading. This technique delays loading images until they are about to appear in the viewport, improving page performance. You will learn to use the Intersection Observer API to detect when an image enters the screen. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and the `useRef` and `useState` hooks to manage image visibility and references.
intro.usecase: Image lazy loading is a critical performance optimization used in virtually any web application that displays many images, such as e-commerce product galleries, social media feeds, or news article listings. For example, an online store like Amazon uses lazy loading to defer loading product images below the viewport until a user scrolls near them, drastically improving initial page load times. As a React developer, you'll implement this to enhance user experience in dashboards with data visualizations or admin panels with media libraries, ensuring smooth scrolling and reduced data usage. Mastering this pattern is essential for building fast, scalable interfaces that handle large sets of visual content efficiently.

objectives: Implement a React component with TypeScript that conditionally renders an image based on its visibility in the viewport.
Initialize and manage component state to track whether an image element is intersecting with the viewport.
Configure the Intersection Observer API to monitor image elements and trigger callbacks when they enter or exit the viewport.
Bind the Intersection Observer to image elements using React refs to establish a connection between the DOM and component logic.
Apply conditional rendering to display placeholder content or a loading indicator while images are outside the viewport.
Control the Intersection Observer's behavior by setting appropriate threshold and root margin options for optimal lazy loading performance.
Integrate the lazy loading image component into a larger application to demonstrate its practical use in improving page load performance.

steps.title: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement or multiple import statements to bring in all the required hooks and React itself.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the required hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have the necessary imports to start building the lazy loading functionality.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required hooks, but make sure to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the ImageGallery component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ImageGallery that returns null for now. Use TypeScript to type the component's props with an interface.
steps.hint: Define an interface for props (e.g., ImageGalleryProps) and use it in the component signature. The component should return null initially.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

// Create the ImageGallery component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed ImageGallery component is defined with an interface for props and returns null.
successCriteria: ImageGallery component is created with proper TypeScript interface for props and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named ImageGallery, has a TypeScript interface for props, and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the component name, TypeScript interface, and return statement.

steps.title: Initialize state for loaded images
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, use useState to create a state variable called loadedImages that will track which images have been loaded. Initialize it as an empty array of numbers.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with a generic type to specify the state type. For example: useState<number[]>([])
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for tracking completed tasks
const [completedTasks, setCompletedTasks] = useState<number[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable ready to track loaded image indices.
successCriteria: loadedImages state is declared using useState with type number[] and initialized as an empty array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the correct type annotation for an array of numbers.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try using useState<number[]>([]) to create the loadedImages state variable.

steps.title: Create image data array
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, create a constant array named 'images' containing at least 3 image objects, each with 'src' (string URL) and 'alt' (string description) properties.
steps.hint: Define the array directly in the component body using TypeScript's type inference. You can use placeholder image URLs like 'https://picsum.photos/400/300?random=1'.
steps.expectedOutcome: An array of image objects is defined and ready to be used for rendering the gallery.
successCriteria: The 'images' array exists with at least 3 objects, each containing 'src' and 'alt' string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your array has the correct structure. Each object needs both 'src' and 'alt' as strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The image data array isn't properly defined. Make sure you create a constant named 'images' with at least 3 objects containing 'src' and 'alt' properties.

steps.title: Create Intersection Observer reference
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, use the useRef hook to create a reference that will hold the Intersection Observer instance. Name it 'observerRef'.
steps.hint: Call useRef with an initial value of null and assign it to a variable named observerRef.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A ref named observerRef is created using useRef to store the Intersection Observer instance.
successCriteria: observerRef is declared with useRef and initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useRef and naming it observerRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to create a ref using the useRef hook.

steps.title: Define image load handler
steps.instruction: Inside your ImageGallery component, define a function named handleImageLoad that takes an image id (string) and updates the loadedImages state to include that id.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setLoadedImages state setter to add the provided id to the current array of loaded image ids.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleImageLoad function is defined that updates the loadedImages state when called with an image id.
successCriteria: The handleImageLoad function is defined, takes a string parameter, and uses setLoadedImages to add the id to the state array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but check that it properly updates the loadedImages state. Make sure it adds the image id to the current array using the state setter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleImageLoad that takes an image id and updates the loadedImages state to include that id.

steps.title: Set up Intersection Observer effect
steps.instruction: Create a useEffect hook in your ImageGallery component that sets up an Intersection Observer to track when images become visible in the viewport.
steps.hint: The useEffect should create a new IntersectionObserver instance and assign it to the observerRef. Remember to return a cleanup function that disconnects the observer.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useEffect hook is added that creates an IntersectionObserver and stores it in observerRef, with proper cleanup.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is implemented with an empty dependency array, creates an IntersectionObserver, assigns it to observerRef.current, and returns a cleanup function that disconnects the observer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect includes both the observer setup and proper cleanup. Check that you're assigning to observerRef.current and returning a cleanup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Intersection Observer effect isn't set up correctly. Remember to use useEffect with an empty dependency array, create a new IntersectionObserver, store it in observerRef.current, and return a cleanup function.

steps.title: Create main container structure
steps.instruction: In your ImageGallery component, replace the current return statement with a JSX structure that returns a main container div with the CSS class 'image-gallery'.
steps.hint: The container div should wrap around where your images will eventually be rendered. Use the className attribute for styling.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element with the class 'image-gallery', establishing the basic layout structure for the image gallery.
successCriteria: The ImageGallery component returns a div element with className='image-gallery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div with exactly the className 'image-gallery'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating the container structure. You need to replace the return statement with a div element that has the class 'image-gallery'.

steps.title: Map through images and render items
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, use the map method on the images array to render each image item. For each image object, return an img element with src, alt, and a ref attribute.
steps.hint: Remember to use the image's id as the key prop for each rendered img element. The ref should be attached to each img element for the Intersection Observer.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will render three img elements, each with the correct src, alt, and key attributes, ready for the Intersection Observer ref to be attached.
successCriteria: The images array is mapped to render img elements with proper key, src, and alt attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each img element has a key prop using the image id, and includes both src and alt attributes from the image object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mapping isn't quite correct. Check that you're using images.map, returning an img element for each item, and including key, src, and alt attributes.

steps.title: Wire onLoad event to handler
steps.instruction: Add an onLoad event handler to each img element that calls the handleImageLoad function when the image loads.
steps.hint: Use the onLoad prop on the img element and pass it the handleImageLoad function reference.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an event handler to an element
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each img element will have an onLoad event that triggers the handleImageLoad function when the image loads.
successCriteria: All img elements have an onLoad prop that calls handleImageLoad with the image id.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an onLoad handler, but make sure it calls handleImageLoad with the correct image id parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onLoad event handler is missing or not properly connected to handleImageLoad.
